Expected precision of a suggested model for a sampling design

Source: R/nm_suggest_design.R
nm_suggest_design.Rd

Computes, before any NONMEM run, the expected relative standard errors (RSE) of the parameters of a candidate model from nm_suggest_model() and the expected eta-shrinkage, for the sampling design of the dataset or for another design. The population Fisher information matrix is computed with the first-order (FO) approximation, block-diagonal between fixed effects and variance parameters (as in PopED's reduced FIM), with numerical derivatives; predictions use the analytic solution of the linear model, with superposition of all doses (ADDL/II expanded). The expected shrinkage of each ETA is 1 - sqrt(1 - mean(C_kk / omega_k)), where C is the posterior covariance of the ETAs of each subject in the linearised model.

Usage

nm_suggest_design(x, candidate = 1L, times = NULL, n_subjects = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'nm_suggest_design'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nm_suggest_design'
plot(x, ...)

Arguments

x

An nm_model_suggestion object.

candidate

Candidate number (default 1).

times

Optional sampling times after the first dose, applied to every subject in place of the observed times (to compare designs).

n_subjects

Optional number of subjects: the information is scaled from the subjects of the dataset to this number.

...

Ignored.

Value

An object of class nm_suggest_design: parameters (parameter, type, value, se, rse_pct), shrinkage (parameter, shrinkage_pct), n_subjects, n_obs, spec, times.

Details

The values depend on the initial values of the candidate (THETA, IIV, SIGMA), which are approximate: they rank designs and parameters rather than predict the RSE reported by NONMEM. Michaelis-Menten candidates are not supported (no analytic solution).

See also

nm_suggest_model()

Examples

ex <- system.file("extdata", "example", "example_data.csv", package = "nmpilot")
s <- nm_suggest_model(ex, verbose = FALSE, design_eval = FALSE, max_profiles = 15)
nm_suggest_design(s)
#> Expected precision: 1 cpt | first-order | proportional error | 60 subjects | design of the dataset
#>    parameter  type   value      se rse_pct
#>           CL theta  5.7200 0.23700     4.1
#>            V theta 55.6000 2.57000     4.6
#>           KA theta  1.1100 0.12500    11.3
#>    OMEGA(CL) omega  0.0975 0.01880    19.3
#>     OMEGA(V) omega  0.1160 0.02340    20.2
#>    OMEGA(KA) omega  0.6930 0.13900    20.1
#>  SIGMA(prop) sigma  0.0377 0.00281     7.4
#> 
#> Expected eta-shrinkage (%)
#>  parameter shrinkage_pct
#>         CL           2.7
#>          V           5.0
#>         KA           4.6
# a sparse design with 3 samples per subject
nm_suggest_design(s, times = c(1, 4, 12))
#> Expected precision: 1 cpt | first-order | proportional error | 60 subjects | design: times given
#>    parameter  type   value     se rse_pct
#>           CL theta  5.7200 0.2650     4.6
#>            V theta 55.6000 3.1800     5.7
#>           KA theta  1.1100 0.1480    13.3
#>    OMEGA(CL) omega  0.0975 0.0259    26.6
#>     OMEGA(V) omega  0.1160 0.0377    32.6
#>    OMEGA(KA) omega  0.6930 0.1930    27.8
#>  SIGMA(prop) sigma  0.0377 0.0159    42.3
#> 
#> Expected eta-shrinkage (%)
#>  parameter shrinkage_pct
#>         CL          12.2
#>          V          19.2
#>         KA          15.1
